title: MineralMinedEvent
description: One accepted extraction: the actor's inventory of this mineral went from quantity_before_kg to quantity_after_kg, and the deposit's remainder went from deposit_remaining_before_kg (after lazy regeneration, ADR-0013 section 1) down by the same amount. Written in the SAME transaction as the inventory row, the deposit row and the processed_commands row (ADR-0013 section 2), so this event is the only explanation an inventory quantity has: for every (world, actor, mineral), inventory = sum(quantity_kg) = the newest quantity_after_kg (spec p1-02 I-54). IMPORTANCE LEVEL 0 - THIS IS NOT A HISTORICAL EVENT (principle 4). The history runner reads it and almost always produces nothing; only the first extraction of a mineral in a star system becomes MINERAL_DISCOVERED (ADR-0014). Rejected MINE_RESOURCE commands produce no event. The schema cannot express quantity_after_kg = quantity_before_kg + quantity_kg or the deposit arithmetic; the server enforces them and QA's ledger identity checks them. actor_id and causation_id are narrowed to non-null.

actor_id.description: Narrowed from the envelope: the actor whose inventory changed. Inventory is owned by the actor, not the ship (ADR-0013 section 1).

causation_id.description: Narrowed from the envelope: the command_id of the MINE_RESOURCE that caused this extraction. The first contract whose cause is a COMMAND rather than an event. It equals exactly one processed_commands.command_id and vice versa (spec p1-02 AC-18(b)).

ship_id.description: Ship that performed the extraction. Joins to SHIP_SPAWNED.ship_id. The ship is where it happened; the actor is who owns the result.

star_system_id.description: Star system of the deposit. Part of the first-discovery key (world, star_system, mineral).

mineral_id.description: MINERAL row obtained, derived by the server from the deposit - never sent by the client.

quantity_kg.description: Kilograms added to the inventory by this extraction: min(the mineral's yield_per_extraction_kg, deposit_remaining_before_kg). Never 0: an extraction that would yield nothing is rejected (RESOURCE_DEPLETED) and writes no event. The history rule's 'actually mined' condition rests on this minimum.

quantity_before_kg.description: The actor's inventory of mineral_id as the server saw it before this extraction. The persistence layer writes the inventory row only if the stored value still equals this (compare-and-set, ADR-0013 section 5); a mismatch stops the world.

deposit_remaining_before_kg.description: The deposit's remainder just before this extraction, AFTER applying the lazy regeneration rule up to this tick (ADR-0013 section 1). Compare-and-set like quantity_before_kg: the stored (remaining, as_of_tick) regenerated to this tick must equal this value.

deposit_remaining_after_kg.description: deposit_remaining_before_kg - quantity_kg. 0 means the deposit is now depleted (a fact the client sees through DEPOSIT_FIELD_STATE; depletion is not a separate event and not historical - design doc section 4.2).
